hypothesis: The sign of BTCUSDT taker order imbalance in the first ten seconds after selected quarter-hour boundaries predicts the same direction of the next twelve-hour return strongly enough for a non-overlapping 1x futures position to retain positive expectancy after taker fees, actual funding, and modeled slippage.
research_basis: Kim and Hansen (2026), The Quarter-Hour Effect: quarter-hour opening order imbalance predicts four-to-twelve-hour returns across six Binance perpetual contracts; sign-based results are qualitatively robust.
The paper explicitly states that its separate ten-second opening-return forecast is too small for a standalone taker strategy, so this experiment tests only the medium-horizon order-flow result.
Binance aggregate trades expose millisecond timestamp, price, quantity, and buyer-maker flag required to reconstruct normalized taker imbalance.

data.source: Binance public-data daily BTCUSDT USD-M aggTrades archives with publisher SHA-256 checksums plus the public USD-M /fapi/v1/fundingRate history endpoint sealed per complete UTC day
data.eligible_start: 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, the first complete UTC day after immutable experiment registration
data.historical_reuse: No observation received before eligible_start may affect a feature, threshold, trade, or verdict.
data.locked_validation: next 60 complete UTC days; must remain unopened unless every development gate passes
data.complete_day: both scheduled twelve-hour holding paths have continuous aggregate-trade IDs across checksum-verified daily archives

pre_result_data_amendments.sample_state: No Alpha #11 archive was downloaded, no eligible observation was loaded, and no feature, trade, or performance statistic was calculated.
pre_result_data_amendments.reason: The Alpha #7 collector intentionally seals and reconnects hourly chunks, which creates unavoidable inter-chunk trade-ID gaps and cannot satisfy Alpha #11's preregistered twelve-hour continuity rule.
pre_result_data_amendments.replacement: Use Binance official daily USD-M aggTrades archives and publisher CHECKSUM files beginning with the first complete UTC day after registration. Require exact archive checksum, schema, symbol, UTC-day containment, unique monotonically increasing aggregate-trade IDs, and no internal ID gaps.
pre_result_data_amendments.unchanged: Signal, direction, clock times, measurement window, holding period, stop, costs, development/validation split, and all gates are unchanged.

pre_result_data_amendments.sample_state: No Alpha #11 eligible archive existed or was downloaded and no feature, trade, or performance statistic was calculated.
pre_result_data_amendments.reason: Official daily archives preserve exchange timestamps but not the collector's local receive timestamps.
pre_result_data_amendments.replacement: After measuring [boundary, boundary + 10 seconds), wait a fixed one-second operational buffer and use the first aggregate trade at or after boundary + 11 seconds as the executable reference price.
pre_result_data_amendments.unchanged: Order-imbalance formula and direction, scheduled boundaries, twelve-hour horizon, stop, costs, samples, and gates are unchanged.

pre_result_data_amendments.sample_state: No Alpha #11 eligible archive existed or was downloaded and no eligible feature, trade, funding PnL, or performance statistic was calculated. A 2026-10-07 pre-eligibility funding response was inspected only as an infrastructure/schema probe.
pre_result_data_amendments.reason: The pre-existing Freqtrade funding feather stopped at 2026-09-16, was not updated by the Alpha #11 acquisition supervisor, and was not cryptographically bound to the forward sample.
pre_result_data_amendments.replacement: For every complete eligible UTC day, query Binance's public USD-M /fapi/v1/fundingRate endpoint with fixed inclusive startTime and endTime and limit 1000; validate BTCUSDT, timestamp containment/order, finite rates, positive mark prices, and Regular/Special type; canonicalize and immutably seal the response and SHA-256 in the same acquisition manifest. Sum distinct Regular and Special rows at an identical fundingTime because both are actual charges at that event. Reconcile against publisher-checksummed monthly fundingRate archives when each month becomes available.
pre_result_data_amendments.unchanged: Signal, direction, clock times, measurement window, holding period, stop, fee/slippage assumptions, actual-funding accounting, development/validation split, and all gates are unchanged.

pre_result_data_amendments.sample_state: No Alpha #11 eligible archive existed or was downloaded and no eligible feature, trade, funding PnL, or performance statistic was calculated.
pre_result_data_amendments.reason: A code audit found that applying a bare funding rate ignores the mark-notional basis of the actual perpetual-futures funding transfer.
pre_result_data_amendments.replacement: For a fixed 1x base-quantity position, calculate each funding event return as -direction * fundingRate * markPrice / executedEntryPrice. Apply every distinct Regular and Special row; rows sharing fundingTime therefore contribute additively using their own sealed markPrice.
pre_result_data_amendments.unchanged: This implements the already preregistered actual-funding requirement; signal, direction, clock times, holding period, stop, trading costs, samples, and gates are unchanged.

pre_result_data_amendments.sample_state: No Alpha #11 eligible archive existed or was downloaded and no eligible feature, trade, funding PnL, or performance statistic was calculated.
pre_result_data_amendments.reason: Aggregate-trade and funding timestamps cannot establish ordering inside the same millisecond when a stop or entry shares a fundingTime.
pre_result_data_amendments.replacement: At an entry/exit timestamp tie, include an adverse funding charge but exclude an ambiguous funding credit. Strictly interior funding events are always applied.
pre_result_data_amendments.unchanged: Signal, holding period, stop level, fees, slippage, non-tied funding accounting, samples, and gates are unchanged.

fixed_signal.availability_rule: the ten-second window is complete at boundary + 10 seconds; a fixed one-second operational buffer is then imposed
fixed_signal.order_imbalance: sum(quantity * direction) / sum(quantity), with direction +1 when isBuyerMaker is false and -1 when true
fixed_signal.direction: imbalance > 0 enters long; imbalance < 0 enters short; exactly zero or no trades emits no signal
fixed_signal.entry: first aggregate trade with exchange timestamp at or after boundary + 11 seconds, with adverse modeled slippage

cost_model.funding: actual Binance funding events while the position is open
cost_model.funding_timestamp_tie_rule: when exchange timestamps cannot order an entry/exit and a funding event within the same millisecond, include the event only when it is adverse to the position and exclude an ambiguous credit
cost_model.stop_gap_rule: if the first executable price after a gap is beyond the stop, exit at that worse price; otherwise exit at the stop; exit fee and slippage still apply

prohibited: using pre-registration observations for warmup, selection, or performance
changing boundary times, ten-second window, holding horizon, stop, direction mapping, costs, or gates after observing results
treating overlapping quarter-hour regression observations from the paper as executable independent trades
opening locked validation when any development gate fails
using archives with manifest, publisher-checksum, schema, UTC-day, or aggregate-trade-ID continuity failure
submitting live or test orders during this experiment
